   297→- **`terraform-validate.yml`** - Validation + Trivy security scanning
   298→- **`terraform-plan.yml`** - Terraform planning
   299→- **`terraform-apply.yml`** - Terraform apply
   300→- **`terraform-drift.yml`** - Drift detection
   301→- **`terraform-test.yml`** - Terratest execution
   302→
   303→### Branch Restrictions
   304→
   305→**Deployment workflows are restricted to:**
   306→- `main` - Production-ready code
   307→- `develop` - Development branch (Git Flow standard)
   308→- `v*` - Version tags (e.g., v1.2.3)
   309→
   310→**Why:** Prevents accidental deployments from feature branches and ensures only approved code is deployed.
   311→
   312→### Branch-to-Environment Access Control
   313→
   314→Deployment permissions are enforced based on branch type to ensure progressive promotion and prevent accidental production deployments:
   315→
   316→| Branch Type | Allowed Environments | Use Case |
   317→|-------------|---------------------|----------|
   318→| `develop` | `dev` only | Development and testing |
   319→| `main` | `dev`, `qa`, `bootstrap`, `shared` | Stable code promotion |
   320→| `v*` tags | `prod` only | Production releases |
   321→
   322→**Examples:**
   323→- ✅ `develop` → `dev` - Allowed (development testing)
   324→- ✅ `main` → `qa` - Allowed (stable code promotion)
   325→- ✅ `main` → `bootstrap` - Allowed (infrastructure management)
   326→- ✅ `v1.2.3` → `prod` - Allowed (tagged release)
   327→- ❌ `develop` → `qa` - Denied (must merge to main first)
   328→- ❌ `main` → `prod` - Denied (requires version tag)
   329→- ❌ `v1.2.3` → `qa` - Denied (tags are for production only)
   330→
   331→**Production deployment process:**
   332→1. Test in `dev` from `develop` branch
   333→2. Create PR: `develop` → `main`
   334→3. Merge and test in `qa` from `main` branch
   335→4. Create version tag on `main`: `git tag -a v1.2.3 -m "Release 1.2.3"`
   336→5. Push tag: `git push origin v1.2.3`
   337→6. Deploy to `prod` from `v1.2.3` tag (during change window)
   338→
   339→**Rationale:**
   340→- Progressive promotion ensures code quality (dev → qa → prod)
   341→- Production deployments require explicit versioning for traceability
   342→- Clear separation between development/test and production paths
   343→- Prevents accidental production deployments from main or develop branches
   344→
   345→### Release Management
   346→
   347→**Manual tagging and releases:**
   348→- Create semantic version tags manually for significant milestones
   349→- Use `git tag -a v1.2.3 -m "Release message"`
   350→- Push tags: `git push origin v1.2.3`
   351→- Create GitHub release from tag via UI
   352→
   353→**No automatic tagging:** Tags are created manually to mark significant releases, not on every merge.
   354→
   355→---
   356→
   357→## GitHub Actions OIDC for Service Repositories
   358→
   359→### Overview
   360→
   361→Service repositories (e.g., kix-services-crewai) use GitHub Actions OIDC for keyless authentication to GCP. Configuration is managed in `environments/{env}/gcp/iam/` with per-environment security controls.
   362→
   363→**No service account keys** - All authentication uses Workload Identity Federation (org policy compliant).
   364→
   365→### Architecture
   366→
   367→```
   368→GitHub Actions Workflow → OIDC Token → Workload Identity Pool → Service Account → GCP Resources
   369→```
   370→
   371→**Per-Environment OIDC:**
   372→- Dev: `github-{service}-dev` pool
   373→- QA: `github-{service}-qa` pool
   374→- Prod: `github-{service}-prod` pool
   375→
   376→### Configuration Location
   377→
   378→**Terraform:** `environments/{env}/gcp/iam/service-deployments.tf`
   379→**Config:** `environments/{env}/config.json` → `service_deployments` section
   380→**State:** `gs://kd-tfstate-{env}/gcp/iam/terraform.tfstate`
   381→
   382→### Adding a New Service
   383→
   384→1. **Update config.json:**
   385→   ```json
   386→   {
   387→     "service_deployments": {
   388→       "github_org": "konecta-ix-services",
   389→       "services": {
   390→         "my-service": {
   391→           "enabled": true,
   392→           "github_repo": "my-service",
   393→           "github_branches": ["main", "develop"],
   394→           "github_environments": ["dev"],
   395→           "permission_preset": "standard-deployment",
   396→           "labels": {
   397→             "team": "my-team",
   398→             "service": "my-service"
   399→           }
   400→         }
   401→       }
   402→     }
   403→   }
   404→   ```
   405→
   406→2. **Apply infrastructure:**
   407→   ```bash
   408→   cd environments/dev/gcp/iam
   409→   terraform plan   # Review OIDC pool, service account, IAM bindings
   410→   terraform apply
   411→   ```
   412→
   413→3. **Get credentials:**
   414→   ```bash
   415→   terraform output github_actions_configs
   416→   ```
   417→
   418→4. **Update service repository:**
   419→   - Configure GitHub environment (dev/qa/production)
   420→   - Add secrets: `WIF_PROVIDER`, `WIF_SA`
   421→   - Update workflow (see example below)
   422→
   423→### Permission Presets
   424→
   425→| Preset | Roles | Use Case |
   426→|--------|-------|----------|
   427→| **basic** | container.clusterViewer, storage.objectViewer | Testing, validation |
   428→| **standard-deployment** (default) | container.developer, artifactregistry.reader, secretmanager.secretAccessor, logging.logWriter, monitoring.metricWriter | 80% of services |
   429→| **full** | container.admin, compute.admin, cloudsql.client, secretmanager.admin, etc. | Complex services (requires approval) |
   430→| **custom** | User-defined | Specific IAM requirements |
   431→
   432→### Security Controls by Environment
   433→
   434→| Environment | Branches | GitHub Environment | Approval | Change Window |
   435→|-------------|----------|-------------------|----------|---------------|
   436→| dev | main, develop | dev | None | Anytime |
   437→| qa | main only | qa | Optional | Mon-Fri 08:00-18:00 UTC |
   438→| prod | **main only** | **production** | **Required (2+)** | **Tue-Thu 20:00-23:00 UTC** |
   439→
   440→### GitHub Environment Protection
   441→
   442→`github_environments` enforces GitHub Actions Environment Protection Rules:
   443→
   444→**What it does:**
   445→- Only workflows running in specified environment can authenticate
   446→- GitHub enforces approval gates before workflow runs
   447→- OIDC validates `assertion.environment == 'production'`
   448→- Full audit trail of approvals
   449→

   535→## Common Workflows
   536→
   537→### Deploying Infrastructure Changes
   538→
   539→**Process:**
   540→1. Create feature branch: `git checkout -b feature/my-change`
   541→2. Modify config.json or Terraform files

   546→   terraform plan

   570→
   571→## Common Task Checklists
   572→
   573→### Cloning Environment Configuration (dev → qa)
   574→
   575→**Context:** Replicate configuration from one environment to another. Estimated time: 1-2 hours.
   576→
   577→**Pre-flight:**
   578→- [ ] Source environment (dev) is stable and tested
   579→- [ ] Target environment (qa) config.json exists
   580→- [ ] Review differences: `diff dev/config.json qa/config.json`
   581→- [ ] Backup current qa config: `cp qa/config.json qa/config.json.bak`
   582→
   583→**Configuration Sync (15 steps):**
   584→1. - [ ] Copy `gke_config.namespaces` section
   585→2. - [ ] Copy `gke_config.network_policies` section
   586→3. - [ ] Copy `kong_gateway` configuration
   587→4. - [ ] Copy `litellm` configuration
   588→5. - [ ] Copy `ingress` (Cloud Armor rules)
   589→6. - [ ] Update `global.environment` to target env ("qa")
   590→7. - [ ] Update `global.labels` if environment-specific
   591→8. - [ ] Review `gke_cluster.maintenance_windows` (adjust for env)
   592→9. - [ ] Verify `global.project_ids` point to correct projects
   593→10. - [ ] Check `landing_zone.network` settings (may differ)
   594→11. - [ ] Review resource quotas (qa might need different limits)
   595→12. - [ ] Validate JSON: `cat qa/config.json | jq empty`
   596→13. - [ ] Git diff: `git diff qa/config.json`
   597→14. - [ ] Create feature branch: `git checkout -b feat/clone-dev-to-qa`
   598→15. - [ ] Commit: `git commit -m "feat: clone dev config to qa"`
   599→
   600→**Apply Infrastructure (Strict Order):**
   601→```bash
   602→cd environments/qa
   603→
   604→# 1. Network foundation
   605→cd gcp/network
   606→terraform init && terraform plan && terraform apply
   607→
   608→# 2. Security
   609→cd ../security
   610→terraform init && terraform plan && terraform apply
   611→
   612→# 3. GKE cluster
   613→cd ../gke
   614→terraform init && terraform plan && terraform apply
   615→
   616→# 4. Kubernetes platform
   617→cd ../../kubernetes/platform
   618→terraform init && terraform plan && terraform apply
   619→
   620→# 5. Kong Gateway
   621→cd ../kong
   622→terraform init && terraform plan && terraform apply
   623→
   624→# 6. Gateway (load balancer)
   625→cd ../gateway
   626→terraform init && terraform plan && terraform apply
   627→
   628→# 7. LiteLLM
   629→cd ../litellm
   630→terraform init && terraform plan && terraform apply
   631→```
   632→
   633→**Verification:**
   634→- [ ] All `terraform apply` completed successfully
   635→- [ ] GKE cluster accessible: `gcloud container clusters get-credentials kd-ix-eur-qa-gke`
   636→- [ ] Namespaces exist: `kubectl get ns`
   637→- [ ] Network policies applied: `kubectl get networkpolicy -A`
   638→- [ ] Kong healthy: `kubectl get pods -n kong`
   639→- [ ] Gateway has IP: `kubectl get gateway -n kong`
   640→- [ ] Health checks passing
   641→
   642→**Common Pitfalls:**
   643→- Forgetting to update `global.environment`
   644→- Skipping terraform plan
   645→- Applying out of order
   646→- Not updating project IDs
   647→- Missing GCP health check IPs in network policies

   680→
   681→## Mistakes Learned
   682→
   683→This section captures mistakes and prevention strategies.
   684→
   685→**Format:**
   686→```
   687→❌ Mistake: [What was wrong]
   688→✅ Correct: [What's correct]
   689→Why: [Impact]
   690→When Fixed: [Date]
   691→Lesson: [Prevention strategy]
   692→```
   693→
   694→### Configuration Errors
   695→
   696→#### Missing GCP Health Check IPs (Ongoing)
   697→
   698→❌ **Mistake:** Creating network policies without allowing GCP health check IP ranges
   699→
   700→✅ **Correct:** Always include in `allowed_ingress`:
   701→```json
   702→{
   703→  "network_isolation": {
   704→    "enabled": true,
   705→    "allowed_ingress": [
   706→      {"cidr_block": "35.191.0.0/16", "ports": [{"port": 8080, "protocol": "TCP"}]},
   707→      {"cidr_block": "130.211.0.0/22", "ports": [{"port": 8080, "protocol": "TCP"}]}
   708→    ]
   709→  }
   710→}
   711→```
   712→
   713→**Why:** Load balancer health checks fail without these IPs, causing traffic disruption.
   714→
   715→**Lesson:** Always verify health check IP ranges in network policies before applying.
   716→
   717→#### Applying to Multiple Environments (Ongoing)
   718→
   719→❌ **Mistake:** Modifying config files for dev AND qa in same commit without explicit request
   720→
   721→✅ **Correct:** Only modify the environment explicitly being worked on
   722→
   723→**Why:** Changes may have different impacts per environment. QA/prod require careful change management.
   724→
   725→**Lesson:** Single environment scope rule - ask user which environment to modify.
   726→
   727→### Module Reference Errors
   728→
   729→#### Using Local Module Paths (2026-02-03)
   730→
   731→❌ **Mistake:** Using local relative paths after module migration:
   732→```hcl
   733→source = "../../../../modules/gcp/landing-zone"
   734→```
   735→
   736→✅ **Correct:** Use GitHub module sources:
   737→```hcl
   738→source = "github.com/konecta-ix-platform/kix-platform-modules//terraform/gcp/landing-zone?ref=v1.0.0"
   739→```
   740→
   741→**Why:** Modules no longer exist in this repository after migration to kix-platform-modules.
   742→
   743→**Lesson:** Always use GitHub sources for modules with tagged versions for stability.
   744→
   745→### CI/CD State Management Errors
   746→
   747→#### Backend Prefix Mismatch (2026-02-05)
   748→
   749→❌ **Mistake:** GitHub Actions workflows using full directory path as backend prefix:
   750→```yaml
   751→backend_prefix: ${{ matrix.directory }}/terraform.tfstate
   752→# Where matrix.directory = "environments/dev/gcp/network"
   753→# Results in: environments/dev/gcp/network/terraform.tfstate ❌
   754→```
   755→
   756→✅ **Correct:** Strip environment prefix to match backend.tf pattern:
   757→```yaml
   758→# Strip "environments/{env}/" prefix to match backend.tf pattern
   759→backend_prefix: ${{ contains(matrix.directory, '/dev/') && replace(matrix.directory, 'environments/dev/', '') || ... }}
   760→# Results in: gcp/network ✅
   761→```
   762→
   763→**Why:** CI/CD was reading/writing to different state file than local Terraform, causing massive plan diffs showing all resources as "new" even though infrastructure was unchanged.
   764→
   765→**Impact:**
   766→- GitHub Actions showed incorrect plan (everything as new)
   767→- Local plan was correct (no changes)
   768→- Two different state files in GCS for same infrastructure
   769→
   770→**Lesson:** Always verify workflow-derived backend prefix matches backend.tf configuration. Consider adding validation step that compares them.
   771→
   772→**Reference:** See `claude_notes/terraform-state-mismatch-fix.md` for full analysis
   773→
   774→---
   775→
   776→## Observability Stack (GMP) Quirks and Gotchas
   777→
   778→### GMP (Google Managed Prometheus)
   779→
   780→**Known Issues:**
   781→1. **PodMonitoring Processing Delay:** GMP can take 2-5 minutes to process new PodMonitoring CRDs
   782→   - **Don't immediately debug if metrics missing** - wait 5 minutes first
   783→
   784→2. **Scrape Target Limits:** GMP has per-cluster limits on scrape targets
   785→   - **Check:** `gcloud monitoring metrics-descriptors list` for quota errors
   786→
   787→3. **Label Cardinality:** High-cardinality labels cause metrics to be dropped
   788→   - **Avoid:** User IDs, timestamps, UUIDs as metric labels
   789→   - **Use:** Low-cardinality labels (environment, service, version)
   790→
   791→4. **Metric Naming:** GMP expects Prometheus naming conventions
   792→   - **Correct:** `http_requests_total` (counter with _total suffix)
   793→   - **Wrong:** `httpRequests` (camelCase, no suffix)
   794→
   795→### OTEL Collector
   796→
   797→**Known Issues:**
   798→1. **Memory Footprint:** OTEL Collector can consume significant memory with high trace volume
   799→   - **Monitor:** Set resource limits, use HPA
   800→
   801→2. **Backend Connectivity:** OTEL exporter failures are silent
   802→   - **Verify:** Check collector logs for export errors
   803→   ```bash
   804→   kubectl logs -n monitoring -l app=otel-collector | grep "export"
   805→   ```
   806→
   807→### Debugging Observability Stack
   808→
   809→**Full Pipeline Check:**
   810→```bash
   811→# 1. Check if metrics exposed at source
   812→kubectl exec -n [namespace] [pod] -- curl localhost:[port]/metrics
   813→
   814→# 2. Verify PodMonitoring exists and selects pod
   815→kubectl get podmonitoring -n [namespace]
   816→kubectl describe podmonitoring [name] -n [namespace]
   817→kubectl get pods -n [namespace] --show-labels
   818→
   819→# 3. Check GMP is processing (wait 5 minutes after PodMonitoring created)
   820→gcloud monitoring metrics-descriptors list --filter="metric.type:prometheus.googleapis.com/[metric]"
   821→
   822→# 4. Query metrics directly
   823→gcloud monitoring time-series list \
   824→  --filter='metric.type="prometheus.googleapis.com/[metric]"' \
   825→  --interval-start-time="$(date -u -d '10 minutes ago' +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" \
   826→  --interval-end-time="$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)"
   827→
   828→# 5. Only then check dashboards
   829→```
   830→
   831→**Common Mistake:** Debugging dashboard queries before verifying metrics are being collected.
   832→
   833→---
   834→
   835→## Infrastructure Debugging Protocols
   836→
   837→### Systematic Debugging Approach
   838→
   839→When investigating infrastructure issues, follow this order to avoid rabbit holes:
   840→
   841→1. **Verify End-to-End First** - Don't dive into specific components until you've verified the full path
   842→2. **Use Task Agents for Multi-Hypothesis** - Spawn parallel investigations when multiple causes are possible
   843→3. **Check Apply Order** - Verify dependencies were applied in correct order (network → security → GKE → platform)

   845→### Terraform Drift Detection
   846→
   847→**Scenario:** Infrastructure state differs from configuration
   848→
   849→**Protocol:**
   850→```bash
   851→# Detect drift
   852→cd environments/[env]/gcp/[component]
   853→terraform plan -detailed-exitcode
   854→
   855→# Exit codes:
   856→# 0 = no changes
   857→# 1 = error
   858→# 2 = changes detected (drift)
   859→```
   860→
   861→**Common Causes:**
   862→- Manual changes via GCP Console
   863→- Another user applied different configuration
   864→- Module version mismatch
   865→
   866→### GKE Cluster Debugging
   867→
   868→**Scenario:** Cluster unreachable or pods not scheduling
   869→
   870→**Protocol:**
   871→1. ✅ **Cluster Status:** Verify cluster is running
   872→   ```bash
   873→   gcloud container clusters describe kd-ix-eur-[env]-gke --region=europe-west1
   874→   ```
   875→2. ✅ **Node Health:** Check node status
   876→   ```bash
   877→   kubectl get nodes
   878→   kubectl describe node [node-name]
   879→   ```
   880→3. ✅ **Cluster Credentials:** Refresh credentials
   881→   ```bash
   882→   gcloud container clusters get-credentials kd-ix-eur-[env]-gke --region=europe-west1
   883→   ```
   884→4. ✅ **Resource Quotas:** Check for quota exhaustion
   885→   ```bash
   886→   kubectl describe resourcequota -n [namespace]
   887→   ```
   888→
   889→### Network Connectivity Debugging
   890→
   891→**Scenario:** Services can't communicate or external access failing
   892→
   893→**Protocol:**
   894→1. ✅ **Network Policies:** Verify allow rules exist
   895→   ```bash
   896→   kubectl get networkpolicy -A
   897→   kubectl describe networkpolicy -n [namespace]
   898→   ```
   899→2. ✅ **Service Resolution:** Check DNS works
   900→   ```bash
   901→   kubectl run test-pod --rm -it --image=busybox -- nslookup [service].[namespace].svc.cluster.local
   902→   ```
   903→3. ✅ **Egress Rules:** Verify external connectivity allowed
   904→   ```bash
   905→   kubectl run test-pod --rm -it --image=curlimages/curl -- curl -I https://www.google.com
   906→   ```
   907→
   908→### When to Use Task Agents
   909→
   910→**Trigger:** Infrastructure debugging with multiple possible root causes (3+)
   911→
   912→**Pattern:**
   913→```
   914→Use task agents to investigate in parallel:
   915→1) Whether network policies are blocking traffic (Explore agent)
   916→2) Whether GKE cluster has resource capacity (check quotas)
   917→3) Whether service endpoints are healthy (kubectl checks)
   918→
   919→Report findings from all three before diving deep on any single hypothesis.
   920→```
   921→
   922→**Why:** Prevents wasted time on sequential dead-ends. Parallel investigation identifies root cause faster.
   923→
   924→---
   925→
   926→## Troubleshooting
   927→
   928→### Kubernetes Logs (GKE Autopilot)
   929→
   930→Cannot use `kubectl logs` on Autopilot. Use Cloud Logging:
   931→```bash
   932→gcloud logging read 'resource.type="k8s_container" AND resource.labels.namespace_name="NAMESPACE"' --project=PROJECT_ID --limit=50
   933→```
   934→
   935→### Health Check Failures
   936→
   937→If load balancer shows unhealthy backends:
   938→1. Check network policies allow GCP health check IPs
   939→2. Verify health check port matches container port
   940→3. Check pod is running and responding
   941→

  "new_string": "### Adding a New Service\n\nGroup-level defaults (`default_permission_preset`, `default_github_branches`) reduce per-service boilerplate. Only override what differs.\n\n1. **Update config.json** (minimal entry using group defaults):\n   ```json\n   {\n     \"service_deployments\": {\n       \"github_org\": \"konecta-ix-services\",\n       \"default_permission_preset\": \"standard-deployment\",\n       \"default_github_branches\": [\"main\", \"develop\"],\n       \"services\": {\n         \"my-service\": {\n           \"enabled\": true,\n           \"github_repo\": \"my-service\",\n           \"github_environments\": [\"dev\"],\n           \"labels\": {\n             \"team\": \"my-team\",\n             \"service\": \"my-service\"\n           }\n         }\n       }\n     }\n   }\n   ```\n\n   **Optional fields** (override group defaults when needed):\n   ```json\n   {\n     \"my-service\": {\n       \"enabled\": true,\n       \"github_repo\": \"my-service\",\n       \"github_environments\": [\"dev\"],\n       \"permission_preset\": \"custom\",\n       \"custom_roles\": [\n         \"roles/iam.serviceAccountAdmin\",\n         \"roles/storage.admin\"\n       ],\n       \"cross_project_access\": {\n         \"kd-ix-eur-dev-platform-data\": [\n           \"roles/cloudsql.admin\"\n         ]\n       },\n       \"state_bucket\": {\n         \"enabled\": true\n       },\n       \"labels\": { \"team\": \"my-team\", \"service\": \"my-service\" }\n     }\n   }\n   ```\n\n2. **Apply infrastructure:**\n   ```bash\n   cd environments/dev/gcp/iam\n   terraform plan   # Review OIDC pool, service account, IAM bindings\n   terraform apply\n   ```\n\n3. **Get credentials:**\n   ```bash\n   terraform output github_actions_configs\n   ```\n\n4. **Update service repository:**\n   - Configure GitHub environment (dev/qa/production)\n   - Add secrets: `WIF_PROVIDER`, `WIF_SA`\n   - Update workflow (see example below)\n\n### Adding a New App\n\nApps follow the same pattern as services but use the `app_deployments` section and the `konecta-ix-apps` GitHub org.\n\n1. **Update config.json:**\n   ```json\n   {\n     \"app_deployments\": {\n       \"github_org\": \"konecta-ix-apps\",\n       \"default_permission_preset\": \"standard-deployment\",\n       \"default_github_branches\": [\"main\", \"develop\"],\n       \"apps\": {\n         \"my-app\": {\n           \"enabled\": true,\n           \"github_repo\": \"my-app\",\n           \"github_environments\": [\"dev\"],\n           \"labels\": {\n             \"team\": \"apps-team\",\n             \"service\": \"my-app\"\n           }\n         }\n       }\n     }\n   }\n   ```\n\n2. **Apply and get credentials** (same as services):\n   ```bash\n   cd environments/dev/gcp/iam\n   terraform plan && terraform apply\n   terraform output app_github_actions_configs\n   ```"
}

  "new_string": "### Important Notes\n\n- **No \"full\" preset in production** without explicit security review\n- **Cross-project access** requires documentation in PR\n- **Production deployments** only during change windows\n- **GitHub environment protection** is mandatory for production\n- **Audit logs** automatically enabled for all IAM operations\n- **STS API required** - `sts.googleapis.com` must be enabled on any project using Workload Identity Federation (included in `common_services` in `base-environment.json`)\n- **State buckets** - Services/apps with `state_bucket.enabled = true` get `roles/storage.objectAdmin` on the shared state bucket (`kd-tfstate-services-{env}` or `kd-tfstate-apps-{env}`)"
}

This replaces service account keys with GitHub Actions OIDC tokens validated against Workload Identity Federation.\n\n### Features\n\n- **No Service Account Keys** - Workload Identity Federation only\n- **Per-Environment Security** - Separate OIDC pools for dev/qa/prod\n- **Environment Protection** - GitHub approval gates for production\n- **Least Privilege** - Three permission presets (basic, standard, full)\n- **Full Audit Trail** - Cloud Audit Logs integration\n\n### Supported Environments\n\n| Environment | Branch Restrictions | Approval Gate | Change Window |\n|-------------|-------------------|---------------|---------------|\n| dev | main, develop | None | Anytime |\n| qa | main only | Optional | Mon-Fri 08:00-18:00 UTC |\n| prod | main only | Required (2+) | Tue-Thu 20:00-23:00 UTC |\n\n### Adding a Service\n\n1.   "new_string": "## GitHub Actions OIDC Authentication\n\nService and app repositories use **keyless OIDC authentication** to deploy to GCP. This replaces service account keys with GitHub Actions OIDC tokens validated against Workload Identity Federation.\n\n### Features\n\n- **No Service Account Keys** - Workload Identity Federation only\n- **Per-Environment Security** - Separate OIDC pools for dev/qa/prod\n- **Environment Protection** - GitHub approval gates for production\n- **Permission Presets** - basic, standard-deployment, full, or custom with explicit roles\n- **Multi-Org Support** - Services (`konecta-ix-services`) and apps (`konecta-ix-apps`) in separate GitHub orgs\n- **Cross-Project Access** - IAM roles on other projects (e.g., Cloud SQL in data project)\n- **Service State Buckets** - Optional shared Terraform state buckets per deployment type\n- **Full Audit Trail** - Cloud Audit Logs integration\n\n### Supported Environments\n\n| Environment | Branch Restrictions | Approval Gate | Change Window |\n|-------------|-------------------|---------------|---------------|\n| dev | main, develop | None | Anytime |\n| qa | main only | Optional | Mon-Fri 08:00-18:00 UTC |\n| prod | main only | Required (2+) | Tue-Thu 20:00-23:00 UTC |\n\n### Adding a Service or App\n\n1. Update `environments/{env}/config.json` → `service_deployments.services` or `app_deployments.apps`\n2. Deploy OIDC infrastructure: `cd environments/{env}/gcp/iam && terraform apply`\n3. Configure GitHub environment with protection rules\n4. Add secrets to service/app repository: `WIF_PROVIDER`, `WIF_SA`\n5. Update GitHub Actions workflow to use OIDC authentication\n\n**See:** [CLAUDE.md - GitHub Actions OIDC](./CLAUDE.md#github-actions-oidc-for-service-repositories) for comprehensive guide."
}

     1→# KIX Platform Infrastructure
     2→
     3→Infrastructure deployment configurations for the **KIX Platform** (Konecta Intelligence eXchange) on Google Cloud Platform.
     4→
     5→## Quick Links
     6→
     7→| Document | Description |
     8→|----------|-------------|
     9→| [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md) | Claude Code operational guide |
    10→| [Module Catalog](https://github.com/konecta-ix-platform/kix-platform-modules) | Reusable Terraform/Helm modules |
    11→| [Platform Documentation](https://github.com/konecta-ix-platform/kix-platform-docs) | Full platform documentation |
    12→
    13→## Repository Purpose
    14→
    15→This repository contains environment-specific infrastructure configurations that deploy GCP resources using reusable modules from **kix-platform-modules**.
    16→
    17→**What's Here:**
    18→- Environment configurations (`dev`, `qa`, `prod`, `shared`, `lab`)
    19→- Terraform state management
    20→- CI/CD deployment workflows
    21→- Infrastructure deployment scripts
    22→
    23→**What's NOT Here:**
    24→- Reusable Terraform modules → See [kix-platform-modules](https://github.com/konecta-ix-platform/kix-platform-modules)
    25→- Platform documentation → See [kix-platform-docs](https://github.com/konecta-ix-platform/kix-platform-docs)
    26→
    27→## Repository Structure
    28→
    29→```
    30→kix-platform-infrastructure/
    31→├── environments/
    32→│   ├── base-environment.json   # GCP folder/project definitions
    33→│   ├── bootstrap/              # Creates GCP folders, projects, state buckets
    34→│   ├── shared/                 # Shared services (ArgoCD, DNS, Artifacts)
    35→│   │   ├── config.json        # Shared environment configuration
    36→│   │   ├── gcp/               # GCP resources (network, security, gke, iam)
    37→│   │   └── kubernetes/        # K8s resources (ArgoCD, platform, gateway)
    38→│   ├── dev/                   # Development environment
    39→│   │   ├── config.json
    40→│   │   ├── gcp/               # Network, security, GKE, data, IAM services
    41→│   │   └── kubernetes/        # Platform, Kong, Gateway, LiteLLM
    42→│   ├── qa/                    # QA environment (mirrors prod)
    43→│   │   ├── config.json
    44→│   │   ├── gcp/               # Network, security, GKE, data, IAM services
    45→│   │   └── kubernetes/        # Platform, Kong, Gateway, LiteLLM
    46→│   ├── prod/                  # Production environment
    47→│   │   ├── config.json
    48→│   │   ├── gcp/               # Network, security, GKE, data, IAM services
    49→│   │   └── kubernetes/        # Platform, Kong, Gateway, LiteLLM
    50→│   └── lab/                   # Sandbox for experimentation
    51→├── scripts/                   # Helper scripts
    52→├── claude_notes/              # Working memory system
    53→└── .github/workflows/         # CI/CD pipelines
    54→```
    55→
    56→## Environment Overview
    57→
    58→| Environment | Purpose | Projects | Change Window |
    59→|-------------|---------|----------|---------------|
    60→| **shared** | ArgoCD GitOps, DNS, artifacts | `kd-ix-eur-shr-*` | Anytime |
    61→| **lab** | Sandbox for experimentation | `kd-ix-eur-lab-*` | Anytime |
    62→| **dev** | Development and testing | `kd-ix-eur-dev-*` | Anytime |
    63→| **qa** | Integration testing (mirrors prod) | `kd-ix-eur-qa-*` | Mon-Fri 08:00-18:00 UTC |
    64→| **prod** | Production with enhanced security | `kd-ix-eur-prod-*` | **Tue-Thu 20:00-23:00 UTC** |
    65→
    66→## Quick Start
    67→
    68→### Prerequisites
    69→
    70→1. **GCP Authentication:**
    71→   ```bash
    72→   gcloud auth application-default login
    73→   ```
    74→
    75→2. **Terraform:**
    76→   ```bash
    77→   terraform version  # >= 1.5.0 required
    78→   ```
    79→
    80→3. **Required GCP Roles:**
    81→   - `roles/compute.networkAdmin`
    82→   - `roles/container.clusterAdmin`
    83→   - `roles/iam.serviceAccountAdmin`
    84→
    85→### Deploy a Service
    86→
    87→```bash
    88→# 1. Navigate to environment and service
    89→cd environments/dev/gcp/network
    90→
    91→# 2. Initialize Terraform
    92→terraform init
    93→
    94→# 3. Plan changes
    95→terraform plan
    96→
    97→# 4. Apply (after reviewing plan)
    98→terraform apply
    99→```
   100→
   101→### Apply Order
   102→
   103→**IMPORTANT:** Services must be applied in this order:
   104→
   105→```
   106→1. gcp/network        (VPC, subnets, NAT)
   107→2. gcp/security       (Cloud Armor WAF)
   108→3. gcp/gke            (GKE cluster)
   109→4. kubernetes/platform (Namespaces, RBAC, network policies)
   110→5. kubernetes/kong    (Kong API Gateway)
   111→6. kubernetes/gateway (GKE Gateway + Cloud Armor)
   112→7. kubernetes/litellm (LiteLLM proxy)
   113→```
   114→
   115→## Configuration Management
   116→
   117→All environment configuration is driven by `config.json` files:
   118→
   119→```hcl
   120→# Terraform loads config.json as single source of truth
   121→locals {
   122→  config = jsondecode(file("${path.module}/../config.json"))
   123→}
   124→
   125→# Access configuration values
   126→project_id  = local.config.global.project_ids.network
   127→environment = local.config.global.environment
   128→```
   129→
   130→**Editing config.json:**
   131→
   132→1. Modify the JSON file
   133→2. Validate syntax: `jq empty < config.json`
   134→3. Run `terraform plan` to preview changes
   135→4. Apply via PR or manual deployment
   136→
   137→## Module Sources
   138→
   139→All modules are sourced from [kix-platform-modules](https://github.com/konecta-ix-platform/kix-platform-modules):
   140→
   141→```hcl
   142→module "landing_zone" {
   143→  source = "github.com/konecta-ix-platform/kix-platform-modules//terraform/gcp/landing-zone?ref=v1.0.0"
   144→
   145→  project_id  = local.config.global.project_ids.network
   146→  environment = local.config.global.environment
   147→  # ... configuration from config.json
   148→}
   149→```
   150→
   151→**Module Versioning:**
   152→- **Development:** `?ref=main` (latest)
   153→- **QA/Prod:** `?ref=v1.0.0` (stable tagged versions)
   154→
   155→## CI/CD Pipeline
   156→
   157→**Deployment Policy:** Merging to main **DOES NOT** auto-deploy infrastructure.
   158→
   159→### Workflows
   160→
   161→| Workflow | Trigger | Purpose |
   162→|----------|---------|---------|
   163→| `pull-request.yml` | PR creation | Fast validation + plan (~10 min) |
   164→| `main-validation.yml` | Push to main | Validation only, no deployment |
   165→| `deploy.yml` | **Manual** | Production deployment with approvals |
   166→| `nightly-quality.yml` | Scheduled (02:00 UTC) | Drift detection |
   167→
   168→### Deploying Infrastructure
   169→
   170→**Via GitHub Actions (Recommended):**
   171→
   172→1. Navigate to **Actions** → `deploy.yml`
   173→2. Click "Run workflow"
   174→3. Select:
   175→   - **Environment:** dev / qa / prod
   176→   - **Service path:** e.g., `gcp/network`
   177→4. Confirm and approve
   178→
   179→**Via CLI (Development):**
   180→
   181→```bash
   182→cd environments/dev/gcp/network
   183→terraform init
   184→terraform plan
   185→terraform apply
   186→```
   187→
   188→## GitHub Actions OIDC Authentication
   189→
   190→Service repositories use **keyless OIDC authentication** to deploy to GCP. This replaces service account keys with GitHub Actions OIDC tokens validated against Workload Identity Federation.
   191→
   192→### Features
   193→
   194→- **No Service Account Keys** - Workload Identity Federation only
   195→- **Per-Environment Security** - Separate OIDC pools for dev/qa/prod
   196→- **Environment Protection** - GitHub approval gates for production
   197→- **Least Privilege** - Three permission presets (basic, standard, full)
   198→- **Full Audit Trail** - Cloud Audit Logs integration
   199→
   200→### Supported Environments
   201→
   202→| Environment | Branch Restrictions | Approval Gate | Change Window |
   203→|-------------|-------------------|---------------|---------------|
   204→| dev | main, develop | None | Anytime |
   205→| qa | main only | Optional | Mon-Fri 08:00-18:00 UTC |
   206→| prod | main only | Required (2+) | Tue-Thu 20:00-23:00 UTC |
   207→
   208→### Adding a Service
   209→
   210→1. Update `environments/{env}/config.json` with service configuration
   211→2. Deploy OIDC infrastructure: `cd environments/{env}/gcp/iam && terraform apply`
   212→3. Configure GitHub environment with protection rules
   213→4. Add secrets to service repository: `WIF_PROVIDER`, `WIF_SA`
   214→5. Update GitHub Actions workflow to use OIDC authentication
   215→
   216→**See:** [CLAUDE.md - GitHub Actions OIDC](./CLAUDE.md#github-actions-oidc-for-service-repositories) for comprehensive guide.
   217→
   218→## State Management
   219→
   220→Terraform state is stored in GCS buckets with isolated state per service:
   221→
   222→**Bucket Pattern:** `kd-tfstate-{environment}`
   223→**State Key Pattern:** `{environment}/{service}/terraform.tfstate`
   224→
   225→**Examples:**
   226→- `gs://kd-tfstate-dev/network/terraform.tfstate`
   227→- `gs://kd-tfstate-prod/gke/terraform.tfstate`
   228→
   229→**Benefits:**
   230→- Reduced blast radius (service-level isolation)
   231→- Team ownership separation
   232→- Faster plan/apply operations
   233→
   234→## Security Requirements
   235→
   236→All deployments enforce KIX Platform security standards:
   237→
   238→- **Workload Identity Only** - No service account keys
   239→- **EU Data Residency** - Resources only in `europe-west1`, `europe-west4`
   240→- **Domain-Restricted IAM** - `@konecta-group.com` only
   241→- **Network Isolation** - Default-deny with explicit allow rules
   242→- **GDPR Compliance** - Required labeling and audit logging
   243→
   244→See [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md) for detailed security requirements.
   245→
   246→## Common Tasks
   247→
   248→### Clone Environment Configuration (dev → qa)
   249→
   250→**Process:**
   251→1. Backup target config: `cp qa/config.json qa/config.json.bak`
   252→2. Copy sections from dev/config.json to qa/config.json
   253→3. Update environment-specific values (project IDs, environment name)
   254→4. Validate: `jq empty < qa/config.json`
   255→5. Apply in order (see "Apply Order" above)
   256→
   257→**See:** [CLAUDE.md - Common Task Checklists](CLAUDE.md#common-task-checklists) for detailed steps.
   258→
   259→### Update Module Version
   260→
   261→```bash
   262→# 1. Update module source
   263→# Change: ?ref=v1.0.0 → ?ref=v1.1.0
   264→
   265→# 2. Upgrade Terraform modules
   266→terraform init -upgrade
   267→
   268→# 3. Review changes
   269→terraform plan
   270→
   271→# 4. Apply (test in dev first)
   272→terraform apply
   273→```
   274→
   275→### Debug Network Policy Issues
   276→
   277→**Symptoms:** Load balancer unhealthy, pods can't communicate
   278→
   279→**Solution:**
   280→1. Check GCP health check IPs allowed: `35.191.0.0/16`, `130.211.0.0/22`
   281→2. Verify pod labels match network policy selectors
   282→3. Check network policy: `kubectl get networkpolicy -n <namespace>`
   283→4. Test connectivity: `kubectl exec -it <pod> -- curl <target>`
   284→
   285→**See:** [CLAUDE.md - Troubleshooting](CLAUDE.md#troubleshooting) for more details.
   286→
   287→## Working with Claude Code
   288→
   289→This repository includes [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md) with operational guidance for Claude Code:
   290→
   291→- **Challenge and Validation Protocol** - Always prove work before claiming "done"
   292→- **When to Use Plan Mode** - Complex operations requiring planning
   293→- **Self-Documentation Rule** - Learn from mistakes systematically
   294→- **Operational Rules** - Terraform workflow, environment scope, configuration management
   295→- **Common Task Checklists** - Step-by-step guides for frequent operations
   296→- **Mistakes Learned** - Institutional knowledge from past errors
   297→
   298→## Change Windows
   299→
   300→Production deployments are restricted to specific time windows:
   301→
   302→| Environment | Window | Notes |
   303→|-------------|--------|-------|
   304→| dev | Anytime | Unrestricted |
   305→| qa | Mon-Fri 08:00-18:00 UTC | Business hours |
   306→| prod | **Tue-Thu 20:00-23:00 UTC** | **Restricted window** |
   307→
   308→The CI/CD pipeline enforces these windows automatically.
   309→
   310→## Support
   311→
   312→- **Issues:** Use GitHub Issues for infrastructure problems
   313→- **Documentation:** See [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md) for operational guidance
   314→- **Platform Docs:** Visit [kix-platform-docs](https://github.com/konecta-ix-platform/kix-platform-docs)
   315→- **Questions:** Platform Engineering team via Slack #platform-engineering
   316→
   317→## Related Repositories
   318→
   319→- **[kix-platform-modules](https://github.com/konecta-ix-platform/kix-platform-modules)** - Reusable Terraform/Helm modules
   320→- **[kix-platform-docs](https://github.com/konecta-ix-platform/kix-platform-docs)** - Platform documentation (GitHub Pages)
   321→- **[kix-services-*](https://github.com/konecta-ix-services/)** - Platform service configurations (Kong, LiteLLM, etc.)
   322→
   323→## License
   324→
   325→Proprietary - Konecta Group. Internal use only.

     1→# Bootstrap
     2→
     3→This directory contains the foundational Terraform configuration that must be applied before any environment-specific infrastructure.
     4→
     5→## What Bootstrap Creates
     6→
     7→1. **GCP Folder Hierarchy** - Organization structure defined in `base-environment.json`
     8→2. **GCP Projects** - All projects with enabled APIs defined in `base-environment.json`
     9→3. **Terraform State Buckets** - One per environment (lab, dev, qa, prod)
    10→
    11→## Prerequisites
    12→
    13→Before running bootstrap, ensure you have:
    14→
    15→1. **GCP Organization Access**
    16→   - `roles/resourcemanager.folderAdmin` on the root folder
    17→   - `roles/resourcemanager.projectCreator` on the organization
    18→   - `roles/billing.admin` on the billing account
    19→
    20→2. **Bootstrap State Bucket** (manual creation required)
    21→
    22→   The bucket name is defined in `../base-environment.json` under `bootstrap.state_bucket`.
    23→
    24→   ```bash
    25→   # Replace PROJECT_ID with your state bucket project
    26→   export PROJECT_ID="your-state-bucket-project"
    27→
    28→   # Bucket name from base-environment.json: kd-tfstate-bootstrap
    29→   gsutil mb -p $PROJECT_ID -l EU gs://kd-tfstate-bootstrap
    30→   gsutil versioning set on gs://kd-tfstate-bootstrap
    31→   gsutil uniformbucketlevelaccess set on gs://kd-tfstate-bootstrap
    32→   ```
    33→
    34→3. **GCP Authentication**
    35→   ```bash
    36→   gcloud auth application-default login
    37→   ```
    38→
    39→## Security Requirements
    40→
    41→**CRITICAL:** This module enforces the following security requirements per organization policy:
    42→
    43→- **Domain-Restricted IAM** - All IAM members must be from `konecta-group.com`
    44→- **EU Data Residency** - State buckets created in EU regions only
    45→- **Audit Logging** - All state bucket operations are logged
    46→- **Versioning** - State bucket versioning enabled for recovery
    47→- **Uniform Bucket Access** - Uniform bucket-level access enforced
    48→- **Public Access Prevention** - State buckets are not publicly accessible
    49→
    50→**Reference:** See `/CLAUDE.md` section "Critical Security Requirements"
    51→
    52→## Required Variables
    53→
    54→Create `terraform.tfvars` from the example:
    55→
    56→```bash
    57→cp terraform.tfvars.example terraform.tfvars
    58→```
    59→
    60→Edit `terraform.tfvars` with your values:
    61→
    62→| Variable | Description | Example |
    63→|----------|-------------|---------|
    64→| `org_id` | GCP Organization ID | `"123456789012"` |
    65→| `billing_account` | Billing account ID | `"XXXXXX-XXXXXX-XXXXXX"` |
    66→| `root_folder_id` | Root folder ID | `"folders/123456789012"` |
    67→| `state_bucket_project_id` | Project for state buckets | `"kd-ix-eur-admin"` |
    68→
    69→## Deployment
    70→
    71→```bash
    72→# Initialize (first time only)
    73→terraform init
    74→
    75→# Review planned changes
    76→terraform plan -var-file="terraform.tfvars"
    77→
    78→# Apply changes
    79→terraform apply -var-file="terraform.tfvars"
    80→```
    81→
    82→## Outputs
    83→
    84→After successful deployment, bootstrap provides:
    85→
    86→- `folder_ids` - Map of folder paths to folder IDs
    87→- `project_ids` - List of all created project IDs
    88→- `state_bucket_names` - Map of environment names to state bucket names
    89→- `projects_by_environment` - Projects grouped by environment
    90→- `projects_by_function` - Projects grouped by function (gke, data, security, etc.)
    91→
    92→## Configuration Files
    93→
    94→- `main.tf` - Provider configuration, base-environment module, state buckets
    95→- `variables.tf` - Input variable definitions
    96→- `outputs.tf` - Output definitions for downstream consumption
    97→- `versions.tf` - Terraform and provider version constraints
    98→- `backend.tf` - GCS backend configuration
    99→- `terraform.tfvars.example` - Example variable values
   100→
   101→## Directory Structure Created
   102→
   103→```
   104→GCP Organization
   105→└── Root Folder (var.root_folder_id)
   106→    ├── shared-services/
   107→    │   └── kd-ix-eur-shr-artifacts
   108→    ├── lab/
   109→    ├── dev/
   110→    │   ├── foundation/
   111→    │   │   ├── kd-ix-eur-dev-network
   112→    │   │   └── kd-ix-eur-dev-security
   113→    │   ├── platform/
   114→    │   │   ├── kd-ix-eur-dev-gke
   115→    │   │   └── kd-ix-eur-dev-platform-data
   116→    │   └── workloads/
   117→    │       └── kd-ix-eur-dev-workloads-data
   118→    ├── qa/
   119→    │   ├── foundation/
   120→    │   │   ├── kd-ix-eur-qa-network
   121→    │   │   └── kd-ix-eur-qa-security
   122→    │   ├── platform/
   123→    │   │   ├── kd-ix-eur-qa-gke
   124→    │   │   └── kd-ix-eur-qa-platform-data
   125→    │   └── workloads/
   126→    │       └── kd-ix-eur-qa-workloads-data
   127→    └── prod/
   128→        ├── foundation/
   129→        │   ├── kd-ix-eur-prod-network
   130→        │   └── kd-ix-eur-prod-security
   131→        ├── platform/
   132→        │   ├── kd-ix-eur-prod-gke
   133→        │   └── kd-ix-eur-prod-platform-data
   134→        └── workloads/
   135→            └── kd-ix-eur-prod-workloads-data
   136→```
   137→
   138→**Naming Convention:** `kd-ix-<region>-<env>-<resource>`
   139→- `kd` - Konecta Digital
   140→- `ix` - Intelligence eXchange (KIX platform)
   141→- `<region>` - GCP region code (e.g., `eur` for europe-west1)
   142→- `<env>` - Environment: `shr` (shared), `lab`, `dev`, `qa`, `prod`
   143→- `<resource>` - Resource type (network, security, gke, platform-data, workloads-data, artifacts)
   144→
   145→## State Buckets Created
   146→
   147→| Environment | Bucket Name |
   148→|-------------|-------------|
   149→| lab | `kd-tfstate-lab` |
   150→| dev | `kd-tfstate-dev` |
   151→| qa | `kd-tfstate-qa` |
   152→| prod | `kd-tfstate-prod` |
   153→
   154→## Next Steps
   155→
   156→After bootstrap completes successfully:
   157→
   158→1. **Deploy Dev Environment**
   159→   ```bash
   160→   cd ../dev/gcp/network
   161→   terraform init && terraform apply
   162→
   163→   cd ../gke
   164→   terraform init && terraform apply
   165→
   166→   cd ../../kubernetes/platform
   167→   terraform init && terraform apply
   168→   ```
   169→
   170→2. **Deploy QA Environment** (same pattern as Dev)
   171→
   172→3. **Deploy Prod Environment** (same pattern, with change management)
   173→
   174→## Troubleshooting
   175→
   176→### "Error creating folder: 403 Permission denied"
   177→Ensure you have `roles/resourcemanager.folderAdmin` on the root folder.
   178→
   179→### "Error creating project: Billing account not found"
   180→Verify the billing account ID format (XXXXXX-XXXXXX-XXXXXX) and that you have `roles/billing.admin`.
   181→
   182→### "Backend initialization required"
   183→Run `terraform init` before any other terraform commands.
   184→
   185→### "State bucket does not exist"
   186→Create the bootstrap state bucket manually (see Prerequisites section).

> AGENT

Confirmed the issue. Here's how it works:

1. `base-environment.json` → `common_services` is read by `bootstrap/main.tf` (line 60)
2. Passed to the `base-environment` module as `common_services` (line 91)
3. Module merges `common_services` with each project's own `services` list ([main.tf:111-114](environments/dev/gcp/iam/.terraform/modules/github_actions_oidc/terraform/gcp/base-environment/main.tf#L111-L114))
4. Creates `google_project_service` for **every project** across **all environments**

So adding `sts.googleapis.com` to `common_services` enables it on all ~20+ projects (dev, qa, prod, shared, lab) when bootstrap runs - not scoped at all.

**Fix:** Move `sts.googleapis.com` from `common_services` to only the `kd-ix-eur-dev-gke` project's `services` list, since that's where the WIF pools are created.

Let me create the bugfix branch.

> AGENT

**Yes**, the bootstrap SA should have permission. Here's why:

The `google_project_service.services` resource in the base-environment module already enables 5 APIs on `kd-ix-eur-dev-gke` (container, compute, dns, certificatemanager, iap). The bootstrap SA `terraformiac@kd-ix-eur-shr-bootstrap` must already have `serviceusage.services.enable` or equivalent on that project, since it created the project and manages those existing API enablements. Adding `sts.googleapis.com` as a 6th service would work the same way.

That said - this change still requires running `terraform apply` in the bootstrap tier to take effect, which reconciles all projects. The scoping fix ensures only `kd-ix-eur-dev-gke` gets the new API (not every project).

> AGENT

**Yes, running `terraform plan/apply` in the bootstrap directory will evaluate ALL resources in that state, including the Workload Identity Pools.**

Here's what the plan would show:

| Resource | Status | Impact |
|----------|--------|--------|
| STS API on `kd-ix-eur-dev-gke` | **To create** | Your intended change |
| 4 WIF Pools | **No change** | Already ACTIVE in state |
| 4 WIF Providers | **To create** | Still blocked by org policy |
| 4 IAM Bindings | **To create** | Depends on providers |

The problem is that the 4 WIF providers from [github-actions-oidc-infrastructure.tf](environments/bootstrap/github-actions-oidc-infrastructure.tf) were never created (blocked by `constraints/iam.workloadIdentityPoolProviders` org policy per [OIDC_IMPLEMENTATION_STATUS.md](environments/bootstrap/OIDC_IMPLEMENTATION_STATUS.md)). Running `terraform apply` would attempt to create those providers and **fail on the org policy constraint**, which would prevent the apply from completing cleanly — even though the STS API change itself is fine.

**Your options:**

1. **Target only the STS change** — use `-target` to scope the apply:
   ```bash
   terraform plan -target=module.base_environment
   terraform apply -target=module.base_environment
   ```
   This applies only the base-environment module (projects, APIs) and skips the OIDC resources entirely.

2. **Wait for org policy update** — apply everything together once the org admin adds `https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com` to the allowed providers list.

3. **Temporarily remove the OIDC file** — not recommended since the pools are already in state and removing the file would try to destroy them.

Option 1 (`-target`) is the safest approach to just enable STS without touching the blocked OIDC resources.

     1→#------------------------------------------------------------------------------
     2→# GitHub Actions OIDC Authentication for GCP
     3→#------------------------------------------------------------------------------
     4→# Creates a GCP Service Account with Workload Identity Federation binding to
     5→# GitHub Actions OIDC provider. Enables keyless authentication from GitHub
     6→# workflows to GCP resources.
     7→#
     8→# Security Features:
     9→# - No service account keys created (org policy compliant)
    10→# - Repository-scoped access via attribute conditions
    11→# - Optional branch and environment restrictions
    12→# - Non-authoritative IAM bindings to prevent conflicts
    13→#------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    14→
    15→terraform {
    16→  required_version = ">= 1.5.0"
    17→
    18→  required_providers {
    19→    google = {
    20→      source  = "hashicorp/google"
    21→      version = ">= 5.0"
    22→    }
    23→  }
    24→}
    25→
    26→#------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    27→# Service Account
    28→#------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    29→# GCP Service Account that GitHub Actions will impersonate via OIDC.
    30→# Naming: github-{service-name}-{environment}
    31→#------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    32→
    33→resource "google_service_account" "github_actions" {
    34→  project      = var.project_id
    35→  account_id   = "github-${var.service_name}-${var.environment}"
    36→  display_name = "GitHub Actions - ${var.service_name} (${var.environment})"
    37→  description  = "Service account for GitHub Actions deployments of ${var.service_name} in ${var.environment} environment"
    38→}
    39→
    40→#------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    41→# Workload Identity Pool
    42→#------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    43→# Pool that groups external identity providers (GitHub OIDC in this case).
    44→# One pool per service-environment combination for isolation.
    45→#------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    46→
    47→resource "google_iam_workload_identity_pool" "github" {
    48→  project                   = var.project_id
    49→  workload_identity_pool_id = "github-${var.service_name}-${var.environment}"
    50→  display_name              = "GitHub Actions Pool - ${var.service_name} (${var.environment})"
    51→  description               = "Workload Identity Pool for ${var.service_name} GitHub Actions in ${var.environment}"
    52→  disabled                  = false
    53→}
    54→
    55→#------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    56→# Workload Identity Provider (GitHub OIDC)
    57→#------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    58→# Configures GitHub as a trusted OIDC identity provider with security
    59→# restrictions via attribute conditions.
    60→#------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    61→
    62→resource "google_iam_workload_identity_pool_provider" "github" {
    63→  project                            = var.project_id
    64→  workload_identity_pool_id          = google_iam_workload_identity_pool.github.workload_identity_pool_id
    65→  workload_identity_pool_provider_id = "github-provider"
    66→  display_name                       = "GitHub OIDC Provider - ${var.service_name}"
    67→  description                        = "GitHub OIDC provider for ${var.github_org}/${var.github_repo}"
    68→
    69→  # Map GitHub OIDC token claims to GCP attributes
    70→  attribute_mapping = {
    71→    "google.subject"        = "assertion.sub"
    72→    "attribute.actor"       = "assertion.actor"
    73→    "attribute.repository"  = "assertion.repository"
    74→    "attribute.ref"         = "assertion.ref"
    75→    "attribute.environment" = "assertion.environment"
    76→  }
    77→
    78→  # Security condition - restricts which GitHub workflows can authenticate
    79→  attribute_condition = local.attribute_condition
    80→
    81→  oidc {
    82→    issuer_uri = "https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com"
    83→  }
    84→}
    85→
    86→#------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    87→# Attribute Condition Logic (Security Restrictions)
    88→#------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    89→# Builds CEL (Common Expression Language) conditions to restrict access by:
    90→# - Repository (required)
    91→# - Branches (optional - if specified)
    92→# - Environments (optional - if specified)
    93→#------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    94→
    95→locals {
    96→  # Build branch filter: assertion.ref == 'refs/heads/main' || assertion.ref == 'refs/heads/develop'
    97→  branch_conditions = length(var.github_branches) > 0 ? [
    98→    for branch in var.github_branches :
    99→    "assertion.ref == 'refs/heads/${branch}'"
   100→  ] : []
   101→
   102→  # Build environment filter: assertion.environment == 'dev' || assertion.environment == 'qa'
   103→  env_conditions = length(var.github_environments) > 0 ? [
   104→    for env in var.github_environments :
   105→    "assertion.environment == '${env}'"
   106→  ] : []
   107→
   108→  # Combine all conditions with AND logic
   109→  filters = concat(
   110→    # Required: Repository must match
   111→    ["assertion.repository == '${var.github_org}/${var.github_repo}'"],
   112→
   113→    # Optional: If branches specified, ref must match one of them
   114→    length(local.branch_conditions) > 0 ? ["(${join(" || ", local.branch_conditions)})"] : [],
   115→
   116→    # Optional: If environments specified, environment must match one of them
   117→    length(local.env_conditions) > 0 ? ["(${join(" || ", local.env_conditions)})"] : []
   118→  )
   119→
   120→  # Final CEL condition string
   121→  attribute_condition = join(" && ", local.filters)
   122→}
   123→
   124→#------------------------------------------------------------------------------
   125→# Service Account IAM Binding (GitHub → Service Account)
   126→#------------------------------------------------------------------------------
   127→# Allows GitHub Actions workflows matching the attribute condition to
   128→# impersonate this service account via Workload Identity.
   129→# Uses principalSet to match all tokens from the repository.
   130→#------------------------------------------------------------------------------
   131→
   132→resource "google_service_account_iam_member" "workload_identity" {
   133→  service_account_id = google_service_account.github_actions.name
   134→  role               = "roles/iam.workloadIdentityUser"
   135→
   136→  # Principal set - all authenticated requests from the GitHub repository
   137→  member = "principalSet://iam.googleapis.com/${google_iam_workload_identity_pool.github.name}/attribute.repository/${var.github_org}/${var.github_repo}"
   138→}
   139→
   140→#------------------------------------------------------------------------------
   141→# Project IAM Bindings (Service Account → GCP Resources)
   142→#------------------------------------------------------------------------------
   143→# Grants the service account permissions in the project based on the selected
   144→# permission preset or custom roles.
   145→# Uses google_project_iam_member (non-authoritative) to prevent conflicts.
   146→#------------------------------------------------------------------------------
   147→
   148→resource "google_project_iam_member" "service_account_roles" {
   149→  for_each = toset(local.final_roles)
   150→
   151→  project = var.project_id
   152→  role    = each.value
   153→  member  = "serviceAccount:${google_service_account.github_actions.email}"
   154→}
   155→
   156→#------------------------------------------------------------------------------
   157→# Cross-Project IAM Bindings (Optional)
   158→#------------------------------------------------------------------------------
   159→# Grants the service account permissions in other GCP projects.
   160→# Useful for services that need to access shared resources (Cloud SQL, GCS, etc.)
   161→#
   162→# Example: Service in kd-ix-eur-dev-gke needs Cloud SQL access in kd-ix-eur-dev-data
   163→#------------------------------------------------------------------------------
   164→
   165→locals {
   166→  # Flatten cross_project_access map into list of {project, role} tuples
   167→  # Input: {"project-a" = ["roles/cloudsql.client", "roles/storage.objectViewer"]}
   168→  # Output: [
   169→  #   {project = "project-a", role = "roles/cloudsql.client"},
   170→  #   {project = "project-a", role = "roles/storage.objectViewer"}
   171→  # ]
   172→  cross_project_bindings = flatten([
   173→    for project_id, roles in var.cross_project_access : [
   174→      for role in roles : {
   175→        key     = "${project_id}-${role}"
   176→        project = project_id
   177→        role    = role
   178→      }
   179→    ]
   180→  ])
   181→}
   182→
   183→resource "google_project_iam_member" "cross_project_access" {
   184→  for_each = { for binding in local.cross_project_bindings : binding.key => binding }
   185→
   186→  project = each.value.project
   187→  role    = each.value.role
   188→  member  = "serviceAccount:${google_service_account.github_actions.email}"
   189→}
   190→

     1→#------------------------------------------------------------------------------
     2→# GitHub Actions OIDC Module - Input Variables
     3→#------------------------------------------------------------------------------
     4→# This module enables GitHub Actions workflows to authenticate to GCP using
     5→# Workload Identity Federation (OIDC) without service account keys.
     6→#------------------------------------------------------------------------------
     7→
     8→#------------------------------------------------------------------------------
     9→# Project Configuration
    10→#------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    11→
    12→variable "project_id" {

    23→    error_message = "Environment must be one of: dev, qa, prod, lab"

    25→}
    26→
    27→#------------------------------------------------------------------------------

    29→#------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    30→
    31→variable "service_name" {
    32→  description = "Name of the service (e.g., kix-conversation-api). Used for resource naming."
    33→  type        = string
    34→
    35→  validation {
    36→    condition     = can(regex("^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$", var.service_name))
    37→    error_message = "Service name must start with a letter and contain only lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens"
    38→  }
    39→}
    40→
    41→#------------------------------------------------------------------------------

    43→#------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    44→
    45→variable "github_org" {

    47→  type        = string
    48→  default     = "konecta-ix-platform"
    49→}
    50→
    51→variable "github_repo" {
    52→  description = "GitHub repository name (without org prefix)"

    54→}
    55→
    56→variable "github_branches" {

    60→}
    61→

    66→}
    67→
    68→#------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    69→# IAM Permissions Configuration

    71→
    72→variable "permission_preset" {

    76→
    77→  validation {

     1→#------------------------------------------------------------------------------
     2→# GitHub Actions OIDC Authentication for GCP
     3→#------------------------------------------------------------------------------
     4→# Creates a GCP Service Account with Workload Identity Federation binding to
     5→# GitHub Actions OIDC provider. Enables keyless authentication from GitHub
     6→# workflows to GCP resources.
     7→#
     8→# Security Features:
     9→# - No service account keys created (org policy compliant)
    10→# - Repository-scoped access via attribute conditions
    11→# - Optional branch and environment restrictions
    12→# - Non-authoritative IAM bindings to prevent conflicts
    13→#------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    14→
    15→terraform {
    16→  required_version = ">= 1.5.0"
    17→
    18→  required_providers {
    19→    google = {
    20→      source  = "hashicorp/google"
    21→      version = ">= 5.0"
    22→    }
    23→  }
    24→}
    25→
    26→#------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    27→# Service Account
    28→#------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    29→# GCP Service Account that GitHub Actions will impersonate via OIDC.
    30→# Naming: github-{service-name}-{environment}
    31→#------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    32→
    33→resource "google_service_account" "github_actions" {
    34→  project      = var.project_id
    35→  account_id   = "github-${var.service_name}-${var.environment}"
    36→  display_name = "GitHub Actions - ${var.service_name} (${var.environment})"
    37→  description  = "Service account for GitHub Actions deployments of ${var.service_name} in ${var.environment} environment"
    38→}
    39→
    40→#------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    41→# Workload Identity Pool
    42→#------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    43→# Pool that groups external identity providers (GitHub OIDC in this case).
    44→# One pool per service-environment combination for isolation.
    45→#------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    46→
    47→resource "google_iam_workload_identity_pool" "github" {
    48→  project                   = var.project_id
    49→  workload_identity_pool_id = "github-${var.service_name}-${var.environment}"
    50→  display_name              = "GitHub Actions Pool - ${var.service_name} (${var.environment})"
    51→  description               = "Workload Identity Pool for ${var.service_name} GitHub Actions in ${var.environment}"
    52→  disabled                  = false
    53→}
    54→
    55→#------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    56→# Workload Identity Provider (GitHub OIDC)
    57→#------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    58→# Configures GitHub as a trusted OIDC identity provider with security
    59→# restrictions via attribute conditions.
    60→#------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    61→
    62→resource "google_iam_workload_identity_pool_provider" "github" {
    63→  project                            = var.project_id
    64→  workload_identity_pool_id          = google_iam_workload_identity_pool.github.workload_identity_pool_id
    65→  workload_identity_pool_provider_id = "github-provider"
    66→  display_name                       = "GitHub OIDC Provider - ${var.service_name}"
    67→  description                        = "GitHub OIDC provider for ${var.github_org}/${var.github_repo}"
    68→
    69→  # Map GitHub OIDC token claims to GCP attributes
    70→  attribute_mapping = {
    71→    "google.subject"        = "assertion.sub"
    72→    "attribute.actor"       = "assertion.actor"
    73→    "attribute.repository"  = "assertion.repository"
    74→    "attribute.ref"         = "assertion.ref"
    75→    "attribute.environment" = "assertion.environment"
    76→  }
    77→
    78→  # Security condition - restricts which GitHub workflows can authenticate
    79→  attribute_condition = local.attribute_condition
    80→
    81→  oidc {
    82→    issuer_uri = "https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com"
    83→  }
    84→}
    85→
    86→#------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    87→# Attribute Condition Logic (Security Restrictions)
    88→#------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    89→# Builds CEL (Common Expression Language) conditions to restrict access by:
    90→# - Repository (required)
    91→# - Branches (optional - if specified)
    92→# - Environments (optional - if specified)
    93→#------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    94→
    95→locals {
    96→  # Build branch filter: assertion.ref == 'refs/heads/main' || assertion.ref == 'refs/heads/develop'
    97→  branch_conditions = length(var.github_branches) > 0 ? [
    98→    for branch in var.github_branches :
    99→    "assertion.ref == 'refs/heads/${branch}'"
   100→  ] : []
   101→
   102→  # Build environment filter: assertion.environment == 'dev' || assertion.environment == 'qa'
   103→  env_conditions = length(var.github_environments) > 0 ? [
   104→    for env in var.github_environments :
   105→    "assertion.environment == '${env}'"
   106→  ] : []
   107→
   108→  # Combine all conditions with AND logic
   109→  filters = concat(
   110→    # Required: Repository must match
   111→    ["assertion.repository == '${var.github_org}/${var.github_repo}'"],
   112→
   113→    # Optional: If branches specified, ref must match one of them
   114→    length(local.branch_conditions) > 0 ? ["(${join(" || ", local.branch_conditions)})"] : [],
   115→
   116→    # Optional: If environments specified, environment must match one of them
   117→    length(local.env_conditions) > 0 ? ["(${join(" || ", local.env_conditions)})"] : []
   118→  )
   119→
   120→  # Final CEL condition string
   121→  attribute_condition = join(" && ", local.filters)
   122→}
   123→
   124→#------------------------------------------------------------------------------
   125→# Service Account IAM Binding (GitHub → Service Account)
   126→#------------------------------------------------------------------------------
   127→# Allows GitHub Actions workflows matching the attribute condition to
   128→# impersonate this service account via Workload Identity.
   129→# Uses principalSet to match all tokens from the repository.
   130→#------------------------------------------------------------------------------
   131→
   132→resource "google_service_account_iam_member" "workload_identity" {
   133→  service_account_id = google_service_account.github_actions.name
   134→  role               = "roles/iam.workloadIdentityUser"
   135→
   136→  # Principal set - all authenticated requests from the GitHub repository
   137→  member = "principalSet://iam.googleapis.com/${google_iam_workload_identity_pool.github.name}/attribute.repository/${var.github_org}/${var.github_repo}"
   138→}
   139→
   140→#------------------------------------------------------------------------------
   141→# Project IAM Bindings (Service Account → GCP Resources)
   142→#------------------------------------------------------------------------------
   143→# Grants the service account permissions in the project based on the selected
   144→# permission preset or custom roles.
   145→# Uses google_project_iam_member (non-authoritative) to prevent conflicts.
   146→#------------------------------------------------------------------------------
   147→
   148→resource "google_project_iam_member" "service_account_roles" {
   149→  for_each = toset(local.final_roles)
   150→
   151→  project = var.project_id
   152→  role    = each.value
   153→  member  = "serviceAccount:${google_service_account.github_actions.email}"
   154→}
   155→
   156→#------------------------------------------------------------------------------
   157→# Cross-Project IAM Bindings (Optional)
   158→#------------------------------------------------------------------------------
   159→# Grants the service account permissions in other GCP projects.
   160→# Useful for services that need to access shared resources (Cloud SQL, GCS, etc.)
   161→#
   162→# Example: Service in kd-ix-eur-dev-gke needs Cloud SQL access in kd-ix-eur-dev-data
   163→#------------------------------------------------------------------------------
   164→
   165→locals {
   166→  # Flatten cross_project_access map into list of {project, role} tuples
   167→  # Input: {"project-a" = ["roles/cloudsql.client", "roles/storage.objectViewer"]}
   168→  # Output: [
   169→  #   {project = "project-a", role = "roles/cloudsql.client"},
   170→  #   {project = "project-a", role = "roles/storage.objectViewer"}
   171→  # ]
   172→  cross_project_bindings = flatten([
   173→    for project_id, roles in var.cross_project_access : [
   174→      for role in roles : {
   175→        key     = "${project_id}-${role}"
   176→        project = project_id
   177→        role    = role
   178→      }
   179→    ]
   180→  ])
   181→}
   182→
   183→resource "google_project_iam_member" "cross_project_access" {
   184→  for_each = { for binding in local.cross_project_bindings : binding.key => binding }
   185→
   186→  project = each.value.project
   187→  role    = each.value.role
   188→  member  = "serviceAccount:${google_service_account.github_actions.email}"
   189→}
   190→

   137→  member = "principalSet://iam.googleapis.com/${google_iam_workload_identity_pool.github.name}/attribute.repository/${var.github_org}/${var.github_repo}"
   138→}

   142→#------------------------------------------------------------------------------
   143→# Grants the service account permissions in the project based on the selected

   147→

   152→  role    = each.value
   153→  member  = "serviceAccount:${google_service_account.github_actions.email}"
   154→}
   155→
   156→#------------------------------------------------------------------------------
   157→# Cross-Project IAM Bindings (Optional)
   158→#------------------------------------------------------------------------------
   159→# Grants the service account permissions in other GCP projects.
   160→# Useful for services that need to access shared resources (Cloud SQL, GCS, etc.)
   161→#
   162→# Example: Service in kd-ix-eur-dev-gke needs Cloud SQL access in kd-ix-eur-dev-data
   163→#------------------------------------------------------------------------------

   170→  #   {project = "project-a", role = "roles/storage.objectViewer"}

   173→    for project_id, roles in var.cross_project_access : [

   176→        project = project_id
   177→        role    = role
   178→      }
   179→    ]
   180→  ])
   181→}
   182→
   183→resource "google_project_iam_member" "cross_project_access" {
   184→  for_each = { for binding in local.cross_project_bindings : binding.key => binding }
   185→
   186→  project = each.value.project
   187→  role    = each.value.role
